cards.explanation: The answer is False. In Moses' example the sign or wonder does come about, but the prophet says “Let us follow other gods…” So he gets his prediction right and still points Israel away from the LORD. A good track record is nice, friends, but it's not the whole picture.

The answer is that he tells them to follow other gods and worship them. Moses says the prophet says “Let us follow other gods (which you have not known) and let us worship them…” That's the invitation, to follow and worship gods Israel has not known. It's a big ask, friends, and the sign coming about doesn't change what he's asking.

The answer is that Israel must refuse to listen to him. Moses says “…you must not listen to the words of that prophet or dreamer.” The sign came true, but the message still pulls away from the LORD. Israel isn't told to be impressed, friends. They're told not to listen.

The answer is testing. Moses says “…the LORD your God is testing you to find out whether you love Him with all your heart and with all your soul.” So a prophet with a true sign shows up as a test of Israel's love. That's the word Moses picks, friends.

The answer is hold fast to Him. Moses says “serve Him and hold fast to Him.” He gives six things in all, and holding fast sits right at the end. It's like holding onto a hot tray with oven mitts, friends. Nobody lets go halfway.

The answer is that he urged them to rebel against the LORD. Moses says the prophet “…has advocated rebellion against the LORD your God…” He also says the prophet tried to turn them from the way the LORD commanded them to walk. That's the reason Moses gives, friends.

The answer is True. Moses calls Him the LORD “…who brought you out of the land of Egypt and redeemed you from the house of slavery…” So the rebellion is against the One who already rescued them. That's the weight behind the whole warning, friends.

The answer is their own family or closest friend. Moses names “…your very own brother, or your son or daughter, or the wife you embrace, or your closest friend…” These are the people closest to you. I think that's why this part is so heavy, friends.

The answer is True. Moses says this person “…secretly entices you…” The word is secretly, so it's a private pitch. And it comes from someone close: a brother, a son or daughter, the wife you embrace, or a closest friend.

The answer is False. Moses says “Show him no pity, and do not spare him or shield him.” I think this one is heavy, friends, because it's someone close. The text names a brother, a son or daughter, a wife and a closest friend.

The answer is that he tried to turn them from the LORD. Moses says to stone him “…for trying to turn you away from the LORD your God, who brought you out of the land of Egypt, out of the house of slavery.” The reason is about turning them from the LORD, friends. That's the reason Moses gives.

The answer is afraid. Moses says “…all Israel will hear and be afraid, and will never again do such a wicked thing among you.” So the news reaches all Israel, everyone. They hear it, they're afraid, and Moses says they will never again do such a wicked thing among them.

The answer is to investigate it thoroughly. Moses' words are “…you must inquire, investigate, and interrogate thoroughly.” A report is only a report until it's checked, friends. That's three verbs in a row, so he really means it.
The answer is False. Moses says the action comes only “…if it is established with certainty…” That's why he says to inquire, investigate and interrogate thoroughly, friends. Certainty comes first.

The answer is to burn it along with the city. Moses says to “…completely burn the city and all its plunder as a whole burnt offering to the LORD your God.” The plunder doesn't go home with anyone, friends. It goes into the fire with the city.
The answer is False. Moses says “The city must remain a mound of ruins forever, never to be rebuilt.” That's a heavy picture, friends, with no someday in it. The word is forever.

The answer is His fierce anger. Moses says that when nothing devoted clings to their hands, “…the LORD will turn from His fierce anger…” So Israel holding nothing back changes how this ends, friends. That's what the verse says.

The answer is that the LORD will show them compassion. Moses says the LORD will “…grant you mercy, show you compassion, and multiply you as He swore to your fathers…” Mercy, compassion and growing numbers are all there. I'd say that's a lot of good news after a hard stretch, friends.

The answer is True. Moses says this is “…because you obey the LORD your God, keeping all His commandments I am giving you today and doing what is right in the eyes of the LORD your God.” The verse before it names the mercy: the LORD will “…grant you mercy, show you compassion, and multiply you as He swore to your fathers…” Those reasons are spelled out in the verse itself, friends.
